reasoning: Preserved both failure-driven edits because they add distinct corrective guidance on matching entity level and handling selectors and undocumented enum values. Added the success-driven guidance on exhaustive requests because it addresses a separate issue not covered by the failure patches. Retained each edit's support_count and source_type.

edits.target: - Treat endpoint eligibility as a gate: confirm the endpoint's own operation and schema support the requested result kind and granularity, and can represent every compatible explicit qualifier. A topical neighbor or broader operation is not sufficient. A named provider or source is a hard constraint for that outcome; do not fulfill or supplement it with another provider when a fitting named-source endpoint exists.
edits.content: - Match the requested entity level and property as well as the topic: a result about a related component or sub-entity does not fulfill a request about the main entity, even when the search terms overlap.

edits.target: - Preserve requested search text, identifiers, and constraints; normalize only as the endpoint requires, without dropping meaningful words or substituting one value or geographic level for another. Map explicit filters, counts, pages, sorting, locale, category, and location to the corresponding schema fields, using accepted representations for enums and locales.
edits.content:
- For optional search-mode or entity-type selectors, use the documented choice that matches an entity class or mode clearly identified in the request, even if the user did not phrase it as a filter. Do not choose an arbitrary restrictive value for another selector dimension the user left unspecified; omit it, or use a documented all/any value only when needed to express the requested scope.
- If a schema declares an enum but does not list its accepted values, do not replace a user-stated label with a synonym or guessed canonical spelling; retain the literal term when its meaning is clear, and do not guess when support is unclear. Preserve the spelling and case of named source values unless the endpoint documents normalization.

edits.target: Include optional settings only when requested or clearly implied; use documented freshness controls for “recent” or “latest” and a modest supported result count for “some” or an open-ended list request (such as top headlines), when a count or limit field is available and the endpoint is not fixed-size.
edits.content: - Distinguish exhaustive requests (“all,” “complete,” or a naturally finite set such as all states) from requests for “some”: when the endpoint documents an all/full-results control or limit/pagination setting, use it to cover the requested collection rather than applying a modest sample size. Do not invent caps or pagination beyond documented controls.
